criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (reef monitoring with fluid lensing) and need (bleaching, 30% loss) clearly described. Single spacecraft justified by temporal resolution. Operator/customers identified. References included though limited.

evidence.quote: Earth observation satellite – specifically for coral reef and ocean monitoring
only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle justified with alternatives (Vega VV18, Falcon 9), equator benefit. SSO polar retrograde 600 km, i=97.79°, COEs table with argument of latitude for circular orbit, J2 explanation, period. Maneuver noted as EOL only. Ground station access report with stats ~580s mean, ground tracks Images 4-5. Duration 5 years STK 2025-2030, drag-sail deorbit. STK screenshots support design.

evidence.quote: will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport
Semi-major axis (a) 6971km Earth radius of 6371km plus a proposed altitude of 600km
Tasmanian facility is selected – the Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion synthesizes launch (Vega E fallback Vega C), orbit, ground station, and mission goal (prevent bleaching). Specific to evidence presented, not generic, though brief.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle
The Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory is well-located to receive data from this orbit type constantly and for long durations

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering structure with exec summary, TOC, sections. Figures/tables present but numbering inconsistent (STK 3D view, unlabeled tables). Grammar readable. Fails R15 - Wikipedia cited as source. References formatting inconsistent.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction

technical_issues.issue: Uses Argument of Latitude u=0° instead of standard ω and ν for circular orbit; RAAN 27.33° justified as launch facility longitude is non-standard definition (RAAN should be inertial, not launch longitude).
Selects Vega E (first flight planned 2024, not yet built at report time - acknowledges risk) but does not compute required performance or piggyback mass.
Access report duplicates entry at 13:00:32 and typo start time '9:38:38.911' on wrong date (Feb 2025 vs 4 Feb) indicates STK table artefact; mean duration calculation includes duplicate.

overall: Strong mission concept for GBR monitoring with appropriate SSO choice and Tasmania ground station. Good STK evidence. Presentation adequate but citation of Wikipedia and inconsistent figure labelling lowers professionalism.

feedback.summary: You delivered a strong, well-evidenced GBR monitoring mission with a clear purpose, SSO design, and good STK support. Your Introduction and Main Body are accomplished, and Conclusion is specific. Presentation is adequate - structure is clear but figure labelling and referencing limited your score.

criteria.C1: You did well in Introduction: primary mission of reef monitoring with fluid lensing, need with 30% loss, single spacecraft for simplicity, and users CSIRO/BOM. To reach 10/10, add more detailed literature and deeper discussion of why one spacecraft meets temporal resolution.
criteria.C2: Strong work in Mission Design: you justified Vega E from Guiana Space Centre with alternatives, defined 600 km SSO with i=97.79°, a=6971 km in your COEs table, and used STK Images 4-5 and access stats with Tasmania Mount Pleasant station. For 10/10, add launch performance calculations and complete maneuver analysis.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion effectively synthesizes your evidence: Vega E fallback to Vega C, polar SSO for illumination, Mt Pleasant for long contacts, and deorbit with drag sail. To strengthen to 9-10, expand why this meets the GBR need and note limitations or future work.
criteria.C4: Report structure is logical with Executive Summary and TOC and readable writing. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, ensure all figures/tables are consistently numbered and labelled (e.g., STK 3D views, access table), and replace Wikipedia in Bibliography with primary sources with consistent citation format.

next_steps: Fix reference quality: replace Wikipedia link in Bibliography with peer-reviewed or agency sources and ensure in-text citations match reference list.
Standardize all figures/tables with consecutive numbers, titles, and source notes - especially Images 1-5 and access report - and check Executive Summary overview is concise.
For future designs, add quantitative launch performance and clearer orbital element definitions (use ω and ν for circular orbit) to fully support vehicle and orbit choices.
